_what: Evidence base for the no-wet-lab publication-archetype survey (CLAUDE.md s0: which routes can still produce a result without a laboratory).
_why: trimcrae, 2026-08-12: 'We're constantly running into hard boundaries from not having a wet lab and that kills so many routes. Understand how other no-wet-lab publications for cancer work.'

_retrieval.harness_incident: TWO failures, both recorded. (1) The first pass hit an account weekly usage limit: 40 of 107 agents completed, 67 errored, and the SYNTHESIS STEP FAILED, so the tool's returned result was a truncation artifact and was NOT reported as a finding. (2) The resumed run reached 102 results and 24 adjudicated claims, then DIED when the container was restarted and the session resumed into a fresh one -- diagnosed from PID 1 elapsed time of ~73s, a `--session-mode resume` launch, and no surviving workflow process. The synthesis never ran in either pass. Everything here was recovered from journal.jsonl by correlating each verifier agentId to its '## Claim under review' prompt. THIRD PASS: resumed again 2026-08-12 and COMPLETED -- 107/107 agents, 0 errors, and the synthesis ran. Its output is recorded verbatim under harness_synthesis below and is the authority over the earlier hand-recovered reading wherever the two differ.
_retrieval.verification_status: 24 claims carry a real 3-vote adjudicated verdict: 16 CONFIRMED, 8 REFUTED (see adjudicated_claims). The remaining ~91 extracted claims have NO verdict because their voters errored on the usage limit or died with the container. An errored vote is neither a refutation nor a confirmation (CLAUDE.md s4).

verified_confirmed.claim: CACHE's defining credibility mechanism is a PROSPECTIVE experimental arm: unlike CASP, CACHE centrally procures and assays the compounds participants predict, so an in-silico hit-finding claim is tested against a wet-lab result the predictor did not control. Screening data are withheld from other participants until cycle 2 completes, making the prediction genuinely blind.

verified_refuted.claim: REFUTED 0-3: that CACHE covers the ~$25,000-per-100-compounds validation cost for every qualified participant, i.e. that a computational-only researcher gets wet-lab validation at zero personal cost.
verified_refuted.why_it_matters: This was the single most load-bearing claim for 'enter CACHE to buy experimental validation for free'. It did NOT survive verification and must not be repeated. The cost structure to participants is UNRESOLVED here.

verified_refuted.claim: REFUTED 1-2: the framing that the CACHE founding paper asserts no computational method could reliably find potent drug-like binders as of 2022.

seer_access_resolution._why: Two recovered claims contradicted each other on whether the free SEER tier needs an INSTITUTIONAL email. That governs whether BLK-REGISTRY-DUA is real, so it was resolved rather than reported as a tension.
seer_access_resolution.finding: As of 13 June 2025, any requestor with a VALID EMAIL ADDRESS may access SEER Research Data, with no restriction by email provider or by countries of concern. The institutional/organisational email requirement applies to SEER Research Plus and NCCR, not to the base SEER Research tier. SEER Specialized Databases require Research Plus access first, plus a Data Access Requestor at professor/senior-researcher level using an institution-affiliated email.
seer_access_resolution.retrieved_via: WebSearch 2026-08-12 (seer.cancer.gov direct fetch is blocked by this container's egress proxy)
seer_access_resolution.caveat: Recovered via search-result summary, not a fetched page. The base tier is also FIELD-RESTRICTED relative to Research Plus: it withholds SEER registry, county, state-county, month of diagnosis, month-of-diagnosis recode, age at diagnosis up to 99, and PRCDA region.
seer_access_resolution.consequence_for_this_repo: BLK-REGISTRY-DUA is SPLIT, not uniform. The SEER half is retirable by an action trimcrae can take with an ordinary email address. The NCDB half is NOT (see ncdb_puf below). This does NOT reorder RT-POPULATION-REGISTRY, which is deliberately sequenced behind the ICD-O-3 9231/3 contamination question and stays there.

ncdb_puf.finding: NCDB Participant User File access is structurally closed to an unaffiliated individual. Three independent gates: (1) applicant must be affiliated with a Commission on Cancer (CoC)-accredited cancer program; (2) a registrar or CoC Quality Portal primary contact must first designate the person as an 'NCDB PUF Applicant' in CoC Datalinks before the application form is even reachable; (3) a signed institutional endorsement on letterhead from the Cancer Committee Chair is required, and the DUA restricts onward sharing outside CoC-accredited facilities.
ncdb_puf.caveat: Recovered via search-result extract of the ACS PUF pages, not a full page fetch.
ncdb_puf.consequence: This is a COLLABORATOR gate, not a money or IRB gate. It cannot be bought or waived.

sources.title: CACHE (Critical Assessment of Computational Hit-finding Experiments): A public–private partnership benchmarking initiative to enable the development of computational methods for hit-finding — Nature Reviews Chemistry
sources.why: The founding paper for the archetype-1 credibility mechanism: CACHE is modelled on CASP but, unlike CASP, mandates a PROSPECTIVE experimental arm — participants submit up to ~100 predicted ligands per target and an independent lab tests binding. Outputs (screening data, chemical structures, algorithm performance) are released FAIR and unrestricted. This is the canonical answer to 'how does purely computational structural work become credible without the authors doing wet lab': the blind challenge outsources validation to the organiser, so a solo unaffiliated participant can obtain prospective experimental confirmation at $0. Also names LRRK2 (challenge #1) and SARS-CoV-2 Nsp13 helicase as targets. Directly relevant to whether an unaffiliated EMC researcher could enter a comparable blind challenge. Free preprint of the same initiative: chemrxiv.org/doi/pdf/10.26434/chemrxiv-2021-rzq4n. Ch

sources.title: Journal of Medicinal Chemistry — Author Guidelines (ACS)
sources.why: An explicit, quotable journal policy REQUIRING wet-lab validation, which is exactly the constraint that structurally blocks the pure-in-silico archetype at top med-chem venues. Retrieved text states: 'Applications of existing computational methods are not considered without original experimental data that assess the computational predictions'; for virtual screening manuscripts, 'convincing experimental data should be provided that demonstrate true biological activity of identified hits' plus compound purity data. Also discourages QSAR/QSPR on already-modelled sets and high descriptor-to-datapoint ratios. The companion ACS Medicinal Chemistry Letters guidelines add that 'computational analyses are not automatically validated by the addition of a minor experimental component.' This defines the venue ceiling: a no-wet-lab EMC structural paper must go to JCIM / JCAMD / PLOS Comp Biol / bioRx

sources.title: Haste makes waste: A critical review of docking-based virtual screening in drug repurposing for SARS-CoV-2 main protease (Mpro) inhibition — Macip et al., Medicinal Research Reviews (2022), DOI 10.1002/med.21862
sources.why: The single best-cited quantification of the docking-paper-mill failure mode: in a survey of 96 articles reporting molecular docking against SARS-CoV-2, NONE reported experimental validation and 40.6% performed no in-silico validation at all (no redocking/cross-docking, no decoys, no retrospective enrichment). This is the editorial backlash an in-silico-only paper must pre-empt — it tells you precisely which credibility elements reviewers now expect as table stakes (pose-reproduction controls, decoy/DUD-E benchmarking, retrospective enrichment, negative controls) and why bare docking scores no longer survive review. Note: full text egress-blocked from this container; title/DOI/finding taken from the retrieved search result, so treat the 96/40.6% figures as retrieved-but-not-page-verified.

sources.title: Reproducibility, validation, and failure modes across classical and AI-driven molecular docking — Journal of Computer-Aided Molecular Design (2026)
sources.why: Current (2026) methodological standard-setting for what a defensible docking/AI-docking claim looks like, spanning classical and AlphaFold/co-folding-era tools. Retrieved content argues mechanistic conclusions must rest on CONVERGENT evidence — pose inspection plus validation performance plus, where possible, orthogonal data — and names the expected validation battery: cross-docking, decoy-based benchmarking, reproduction of experimentally observed binding modes, retrospective virtual screening. Useful as the citable 'how to phrase the ceiling' reference for an in-silico-only structural chapter, and as a live check on whether Boltz/AF-driven target characterisation is held to the same bar. Springer full text is egress-blocked here; title/journal/URL are from the retrieved result.

sources.title: CACHE Challenge #1: Docking with GNINA Is All You Need (PMC11683865)
sources.why: A concrete worked exemplar of the archetype: a small computational team's blind CACHE #1 (LRRK2 WD40) entry published as a standalone paper whose validation came from the organiser's prospective experimental testing, not from the authors' own bench. Shows what the publishable unit looks like when you have zero wet lab — method description, blind submission, externally measured hit rate, honest framing of what the enrichment does and does not prove. This is the closest thing to a template an unaffiliated solo researcher could follow, and it is open access on PMC ($0). Verify the exact author list/DOI on the PMC page before citing.

sources.title: The present and future of the Cancer Dependency Map (Nature Reviews Cancer, 2024)
sources.why: Authoritative statement of what DepMap can and cannot support — needed to set the honest ceiling for archetype 2 and to justify the small-n framings (cross-disease borrowing, fusion-class pooling) that an EMC paper would need. sources.title: shinyDepMap, a tool to identify targetable cancer genes and their functional connections from Cancer Dependency Map data
sources.why: A concrete $0, no-affiliation-required entry point for the dependency-mining archetype, and an example of the 'resource/tool paper' as a publishable output of pure public-data reuse. The tool combines the CRISPR and shRNA DepMap screens to score, per gene, both the magnitude of growth reduction on knockout/knockdown and the SELECTIVITY of that effect across cell lines — selectivity being the axis that distinguishes a real lineage-specific vulnerability from a pan-essential gene, which is the single most common reviewer objection to dependency dredging. Also clusters genes into functional modules, supporting the 'borrow from related lineages' framing an ultra-rare tumour needs. sources.title: Guyot P, Ades AE, Ouwens MJNM, Welton NJ. Enhanced secondary analysis of survival data: reconstructing the data from published Kaplan-Meier survival curves. BMC Med Res Methodol 12:9 (2012). DOI 10.1186/1471-2288-12-9, PMID 22297116
sources.why: The foundational method for archetype 3's highest-yield variant: it derives a close approximation to original individual patient time-to-event data from digitised published KM curves by numerically solving the inverted KM product-limit equations, using reported numbers at risk and total events. sources.title: Liu N, Zhou Y, Lee JJ. IPDfromKM: reconstruct individual patient data from published Kaplan-Meier survival curves. BMC Med Res Methodol (2021). DOI 10.1186/s12874-021-01308-8, PMID 34074267 (PMC8168323)
sources.why: The executable tooling layer for the Guyot archetype: an R package plus a web Shiny app implementing a modified iterative KM estimation algorithm (modified-iKM) that improves on Guyot 2012, covering the full two-stage workflow — Stage 1 extract raw curve coordinates, Stage 2 reconstruct IPD — plus built-in visualisation, RECONSTRUCTION-ACCURACY ASSESSMENT, and secondary analysis. The accuracy-assessment step is the credibility scaffolding a reviewer looks for (reconstructed vs published survival probabilities, numbers at risk, medians, HRs), validated by the authors through extensive simulation and real-data application. Free, open-source, no institutional access, no DUA, no IRB — the single most executable clinical-evidence route for a solo unaffiliated researcher.

It makes comparative treatment-effectiveness claims (anti-PD1/anti-CTLA4 vs KIT and VEGF inhibitors vs radiotherapy) intended to inform management — proof that a therapeutically relevant clinical claim is reachable with zero patient contact. sources.title: Stewart LA, Clarke M, Rovers M, et al. Preferred Reporting Items for a Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Individual Participant Data: The PRISMA-IPD Statement. JAMA 2015;313(16):1657-65
sources.why: The reporting standard that gets archetype 3 past review, and the document that defines the vocabulary distinguishing true IPD (collected and reanalysed from the original investigators) from RECONSTRUCTED IPD. IPD synthesis is described here as the gold-standard approach to evidence synthesis, which is why the archetype carries weight; the checklist's three IPD-specific additions — methods for checking IPD INTEGRITY, reporting issues that emerge, and exploring variation — are precisely the items a reconstruction-based author must address honestly, since integrity checking cannot mean investigator query and must instead be the reconstruction-fidelity check. Free-standing checklist at prisma-statement.org/ipd; costs nothing, needs no affiliation.

harness_synthesis.summary: Across the verified evidence, the "no wet lab" cancer-therapeutics paper survives review by one of three credibility architectures, not by the quality of its computation: (a) BLIND PROSPECTIVE VALIDATION performed by someone else — the CACHE challenge model, where computational-only teams submit predictions against a ligand-free target and the organizers procure and assay the compounds, which is the only confirmed route to an experimentally-confirmed hit-discovery paper for a researcher who owns no bench; (b) DISCIPLINED PUBLIC-DATA REANALYSIS whose credibility comes from leakage-aware splitting, released code and an honestly bounded claim — exemplified by DepMap dependency mining that cleared peer review at target-nomination level (PAK2/HNSCC, Mol Oncol 2024) and by preserved-site cross-validation for TCGA imaging (Nat Commun 2021); and (c) the PUBLISHABLE NEGATIVE / METHOD AUDIT, where the finding IS the failure of a computational resource and the ceiling discipline is to decline to adjudicate what the data cannot settle (Lim & Pavlidis's CMap reproducibility paper is the model). The dominant failure mode is quantified and canonical: in a 61-paper audit of COVID-era docking repurposing, 67.21% applied no validation step at all and only 2 papers (3.28%) tested anything experimentally, docking score did not track measured potency (best r = -0.335), and the adjacent "network pharmacology + docking" genre has been retracted at scale on publication-integrity grounds — so an unvalidated docking or network-pharmacology paper now carries prior suspicion rather than prior credit. The hard constraint for a solo unaffiliated worker is not compute but VALIDATION ASSETS AND ACCESS: the sarcoma exemplar (PLOS Comput Biol 2019) shows the discovery layer running entirely on free public data (TCGA/GTEx/GEO) while the layer that carried the therapeutic claim — archival tumour tissue, a newly built tissue microarray, and ethics-board approval LUMC B17.036 — is structurally unobtainable without an institution. For ultra-rare disease specifically, the one measured small-n rule is that the floor is analysis-type-dependent: n=5 MPNST survived a supervised class-discrimination analysis and was excluded outright from the survival analysis.

This is the single most citable quantification of the 'docking-paper mill' failure mode and defines the bar a serious archetype-1 paper must clear.

findings.claim: Docking score does not track measured potency, so a docking-only paper cannot legitimately claim potency ranking. In the same review's own benchmark — two Mpro crystal structures (6LU7, 6WQF), five docking protocols, 150 literature-derived inhibitors and 81 COVID Moonshot inhibitors — the single best correlation was Pearson r = -0.335 (p = 0.003) for covalent inhibitors with AutoDock Vina, while noncovalent correlations were near zero or of the WRONG SIGN (positive).
findings.evidence: Verbatim: "The best correlation had a Pearson's r coefficient of -0.335 (p value 0.003) for the covalent inhibitors when AutoDock Vina was used... However, the Pearson correlation coefficients for the noncovalent inhibitors were positive or around zero... For the set of 81 M-pro inhibitors from the COVID MoonShot project, most of the correlations were unexpectedly found to be positive." Docking scores are negative binding energies and pIC50 rises with potency, so the expected sign is negative — positive means anti-correlated with potency. The paper's own hedged operational conclusion is that correlation is "not good enough to fully support using a docking score as a cutoff value." IMPORTANT SCOPE CORRECTION: a stronger version of this claim — that neither docking scores nor MM-GBSA dG could separate actives from the 113 confirmed inactives, i.e. that a docking cutoff can NEVER nominate hits — was REFUTED 0-3. Discrimination actually IMPROVED when covalent and noncovalent sets were separated (best AUC 0.744 for MM-GBSA on FRED poses of noncovalent inhibitors on 6WQF). The defensible claim is about CORRELATION WITH POTENCY, not about total inability to discriminate. Independent corroboration of the direction comes from CASF/CSAR benchmark summaries where 'scoring power' lags 'docking power' and few methods reach Spearman >= 0.5 for affinity ranking.

findings.claim: The canonical editorial criticism of this genre is not that any single prediction was disproved but that independent studies using similar libraries and similar methodology nominate DIFFERENT compounds, most validate nothing, and the accompanying language is overconfident relative to the evidence — the review calls unvalidated predictions "speculative and dubious."
findings.evidence: Abstract text: "Various manuscripts predict different compounds, even when they use a similar initial dataset and methodology, and most of them do not validate their methodology or results." Full text: "Without a proper validation, the predictions obtained are speculative and dubious" and "Overconfident statements and conclusions that are not fully supported by experimental evidence are frequently found in articles that use protein-ligand docking to find SARS-CoV-2 M-pro inhibitors." TWO FRAMING PRECISIONS: (a) 'largely different' is an inference from the review's no-consensus finding, not verbatim; (b) the source is a peer-reviewed critical review with its own benchmark, not literally an editorial, and its evidence base is COVID-era Mpro-specific, so extension to 'the docking-paper mill' generally is a reasonable but extrapolative generalisation. A 2026 J Comput Aided Mol Des paper (DOI 10.1007/s10822-026-00849-8, "Reproducibility, validation, and failure modes across classical and AI-driven molecular docking") points the same way. PRACTICAL IMPLICATION FOR AN UNAFFILIATED AUTHOR: reviewers now apply prior suspicion to this template, so the language ceiling must be explicit (nominate a hypothesis, never assert a hit) and reproducibility architecture (released poses, code, negative controls, protocol validation) is what substitutes for the absent assay.

findings.claim: The adjacent 'network pharmacology + molecular docking' cancer-mechanism genre has been discredited at the level of publication integrity, not by anyone re-running the computation. A concrete identifier-confirmed instance: "Network Pharmacology, Molecular Docking, and Experimental Validation to Unveil the Molecular Targets and Mechanisms of Compound Fuling Granule to Treat Ovarian Cancer" (Oxidative Medicine and Cellular Longevity, DOI 10.1155/2022/2896049, PMID 36062197, PMC9428684) was retracted (notice PMC10412175, DOI 10.1155/2023/9867930, Aug 2023) as part of Hindawi's paper-mill sweep.
findings.evidence: The retraction notice cites "evidence of ONE OR MORE OF the following indicators of systematic manipulation of the publication process: Discrepancies in scope; Discrepancies in the description of the research reported; Discrepancies between the availability of data and the research described; Inappropriate citations; Incoherent, meaningless and/or irrelevant content included in the article; Peer-review manipulation" — note 'one or more of', NOT 'including', which is a correction to the originally supplied quote. No scientific re-analysis of the docking is offered as grounds. Context: Oxidative Medicine and Cellular Longevity was among ~19 Hindawi journals delisted from Web of Science for paper-mill activity, inside a wave of 500+ (ultimately 8,000+) retractions for compromised peer review. TWO REQUIRED SCOPE FIXES: (a) the genre HAS ALSO been attacked on methodological grounds — Frontiers in Pharmacology 2026, "Blind docking methods have been inappropriately used in most network pharmacology analysis," DOI 10.3389/fphar.2026.1566772, reviewing 35 network-pharmacology docking papers — so 'destroyed by provenance, not by re-running the docking' is true of THIS retraction, not of the archetype universally; (b) this specific paper included wet-lab 'Experimental Validation', so it is a FAILURE-MODE exemplar, not a zero-new-data exemplar. A broader claim listing six sibling retracted PMC IDs as proof the sub-genre is discredited at scale was REFUTED 0-3 and should not be reproduced.

findings.claim: CMap/LINCS signature-reversal repurposing has a measured, quantified reproducibility problem: querying CMap 2 (LINCS L1000) with 588 CMap-1-derived compound signatures put the correct compound in the top 10% only 17% of the time (99/588) and ranked it first for fewer than 1% of signatures, against a same-resource self-query control of 83% (486/588) top-10% and 53% (313) rank-first.
findings.evidence: Lim N, Pavlidis P, "Evaluation of connectivity map shows limited reproducibility in drug repositioning," Scientific Reports 2021;11:17624, DOI 10.1038/s41598-021-97005-z, PMC8413422 (preprint bioRxiv 10.1101/845693). Figures verified verbatim. THREE REFUTATION ATTEMPTS FAILED: (i) 'it's a platform artifact' (Affymetrix HG-U133A vs L1000 978 landmarks with inferred genes) does not rescue the method, because the authors report low differential-expression reproducibility WITHIN each CMap as well as between them; (ii) validated successes (RGES/IC50 correlation, kenpaullone in Ebola) qualify but do not contradict a reproducibility problem; (iii) the 2021 date does not stale a statement about what a specific benchmark measured. TWO SCOPE PRECISIONS to carry into any write-up: the source is a primary research paper, not an editorial, and it is one of several critiques (cf. Cheng et al., CPT Pharmacometrics Syst Pharmacol, DOI 10.1002/psp4.12107); and the benchmark task is compound SELF-RECOVERY, which is the necessary precondition for disease-signature-reversal repurposing but not literally the same task — state that as an inference. A stronger sub-claim giving specific rank migrations (parbendazole rank 1 -> 142, withaferin-A 9 -> 196, amylocaine 20 -> 122, salbutamol 1 -> 61) was REFUTED 0-3 and must not be cited.

findings.claim: That CMap paper is also the best available TEMPLATE for the publishable-negative archetype: the authors held their claim inside a ceiling a computation-only critique can defend — they attempted and FAILED to adjudicate which CMap version is correct (a third dataset was mutually discordant with both), raised and answered the competing explanation that both resources may recommend different-but-valid compounds, and converted the negative into actionable usage recommendations rather than a verdict that the method does not work.
findings.vote: [9] 3-0 — verified by live fetch of the primary full text via CI
findings.evidence: Verified by fetching the primary page on a GitHub Actions runner (run 31592017890; artifact committed to origin/literature-cache:literature/cmap-lim-pavlidis-verify/cmap_scirep.txt, 76,110 chars) because nature.com is egress-blocked from the sandbox. All three quote fragments found verbatim exactly once each. Abstract: "We attempted to identify the 'better' CMap by comparison with a third dataset, but they were mutually discordant. Our findings have implications for CMap usage and we suggest steps for investigators to limit false positives." Discussion: "Another possibility is that both CMaps do recommend valid compounds - just different ones" — immediately REBUTTED by the authors ("However, one would still expect that CMap 2 would highly rank the queried compound ... and that was usually not the case"), which is a stronger credibility device than conceding it. Terminal position: "Based on these observations and considerable uncertainty about which, if any, version of CMap is reliable, we make some recommendations for researchers" — then concrete guidance on cell-line relevance and signature size. This is the transferable lesson for archetype 9: an unaffiliated author publishing a route closure should (a) name what the data cannot settle and say so, (b) pre-empt the strongest alternative explanation in the text, (c) end in usage recommendations rather than a verdict. Open access, ~60 citations, Pavlidis lab (UBC).

findings.claim: Public digital-pathology repositories carry a strong NON-BIOLOGICAL site/batch signature that inflates published accuracies, and the fix is a $0 method an unaffiliated researcher can execute. Tissue submitting site is recoverable from TCGA whole-slide images by a standard Xception CNN at one-vs-rest AUROC 0.964-0.998 across six cancer subtypes, versus 0.623 mean for a model predicting site from clinical variables; and re-splitting so no site appears in both folds (preserved-site cross-validation) dropped AUROC for 51/56 (91.1%) predictable features, with 20 (35.7%) no longer significantly detectable and a mean drop of 0.069 (range -0.042 to 0.291) across 58 features.
findings.vote: [10] 3-0, [11] 2-1 — merged; batch-effect core unanimous, the resplit statistics carry a scope caveat
findings.evidence: Howard FM, Dolezal J, Kochanny S, ... Grossman RL, Pearson AT, "The impact of site-specific digital histology signatures on deep learning model accuracy and bias," Nat Commun 2021;12:4423, PMID 34285218, PMC8292530, 204 citations. Verified verbatim against the repo's cached open-access full text at origin/literature-cache:literature/howard-site-signatures/PMC8292530.txt. The authors ADJUDICATED the obvious objection themselves with a single-site simulation: "batch effect, as opposed to biologic subpopulation differences, are the predominant cause of highly accurate site prediction by deep-learning models." TWO SCOPE FIXES: (a) the resplit result is measured on TCGA WHOLE-SLIDE HISTOLOGY IMAGES specifically — do not generalise it to all TCGA-derived predictors (e.g. expression-based) without saying so; (b) corruption is TASK-DEPENDENT, not universal — HER2, lobular-vs-ductal, ER/PR status, KIRC grade, TP53 in BRCA/HNSC/LUAD and BRAF in COADREAD were essentially unaffected. A claim that stain normalization and colour augmentation fail to remove the signature (site still predictable above 0.850 OVR AUROC) was 1-2 and is NOT carried as confirmed.

findings.claim: That same paper prescribes the credibility architecture for public-data ML that an unaffiliated researcher can execute at $0, and does so explicitly because external validation cohorts are often unavailable — stating that this is especially true FOR RARE CANCER SUBTYPES. The method is quadratic-programming-based preserved-site cross-validation; all inputs are public (GDC portal, cBioPortal) and the fold-generation code is on GitHub.
findings.evidence: Verbatim: "When developing predictive histologic models for a large number of features, external validation of every finding can be impractical/infeasible. Furthermore, adequate external validation datasets may not be readily available for rare cancer subtypes. As such, multiple studies have trained and validated models using TCGA with no external validation or only partial validation." Method: "We propose using convex optimization/quadratic programming as demonstrated in this study to identify the split of sites to allow optimal stratification of features of interest" (CPLEX v12.10 in Methods). Data availability: "Data from TCGA including digital histology and the clinical and genetic annotations used are available from https://portal.gdc.cancer.gov/ and https://cbioportal.org." Code availability: "Our code used for fold generation for cross-validation is available from https://github.com/fmhoward/PreservedSiteCV" — verified live (public, Python, README cites the DOI; preservedsite/crossfolds.py builds boolean cvxpy variables with a cp.square objective, i.e. a genuine mixed-integer quadratic program). $0 SURVIVES SCRUTINY: the code imports CPLEX (commercial), but the free Community Edition (1000 var / 1000 constraint cap) covers this problem size (3 crossfolds x 38 sites = 114 booleans in the README example), and cvxpy makes swapping a free MIQP solver a one-string change; TCGA slides + clinical data are the OPEN tier (no dbGaP, no DUA). HONEST SCOPING: the authors' full recommendation set is four-part (report outcome variation across sites; never share a site between train and test; use precision-recall not AUROC on imbalanced data; keep stain normalisation/augmentation), and they explicitly do NOT sell preserved-site CV as a substitute for external validation — they call external validation "the tried and true gold standard" and position their method as an early screen for "which features are unlikely to survive the test of external validation." 'Plus public code release' is the surveyor's addition, not one of the paper's listed best practices.

findings.claim: Secondary reanalysis of public molecular data clears peer review at a TARGET-NOMINATION level in a real journal with no author-generated data apparent: Sannigrahi et al. nominated PAK2 as a druggable target in HNSCC purely from reanalysis of public DepMap CRISPR loss-of-function screens plus reuse of public inhibitor-response data.
findings.evidence: Sannigrahi MK, Cao Y, Rajagopalan P, Sun Z, Brody J, Raghav K, Gimotty PA, Basu D (Univ. of Pennsylvania), "A novel pipeline for prioritizing cancer type-specific therapeutic vulnerabilities using DepMap identifies PAK2 as a target in head and neck squamous cell carcinomas," Molecular Oncology 2024;18(2):336-349 (Epub 13 Dec 2023), DOI 10.1002/1878-0261.13558, PMID 37997254, PMC10850805. Identifiers recovered from four independent indexers. DATA BASIS IS ALL PUBLIC AND ALL FREE — the authors' own repo (github.com/BasuLab2023/DepMap-2023, fetched successfully) lists DepMap 22Q1/23Q2 Chronos gene-effect and gene-probability scores for 63 HPV-negative HNSCC + 24 ESCC lines, DGIdb, Open Targets Platform, GDSC2, PRISM Repurposing, DEMETER2, plus the analysis R script and gene lists; no author-generated assay data is deposited. Even the inhibitor arm reuses public assays: PAK-5339 and FRAX486 responses were "evaluated in vitro in GDSC." The pipeline "prioritized 143 targetable dependencies," then compared inhibitor response between high- and low-dependency lines for 13 targets, reporting dependency biomarkers (wild-type p53, low PAK2 mRNA, diploid 3q). UNRESOLVED: full-text Methods could not be read (all relevant domains egress-blocked), so the presence of any author-generated wet-lab layer in the published version is UNVERIFIED; the earlier preprint (bioRxiv 10.1101/2022.06.12.495566) is described as using publicly available DepMap data without new experimental work. TWO QUALIFICATIONS: the headline framing is the PIPELINE as a reusable template with PAK2 as its demonstration output — slightly weaker than 'a bare target nomination clears review'; and for EMC specifically, DepMap contains NO extraskeletal myxoid chondrosarcoma lines, so transferability is blocked by cell-line availability, not by publishability. No retraction, correction or expression of concern found.

findings.claim: The sharpest exemplar of the SPLIT between what a solo researcher can and cannot do is the sarcoma machine-learning paper: its entire discovery layer ran on free public data, but every headline finding was carried through review by author-generated wet-lab validation requiring institutional assets — archival human tumour specimens, a newly constructed tissue microarray, and formal ethics-board approval (LUMC B17.036) under the Dutch Code for Proper Secondary Use of Human Tissue.
findings.evidence: van IJzendoorn DGP, Szuhai K, Briaire-de Bruijn IH, Kostine M, Kuijjer ML, Bovee JVMG, "Machine learning analysis of gene expression data reveals novel diagnostic and prognostic biomarkers and identifies therapeutic targets for soft tissue sarcomas," PLoS Comput Biol 2019, DOI 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1006826, PMID 30785874, PMC6398862. Verified against Europe PMC full-text XML and a CI-fetched copy (run 31594039131; origin/literature-cache:literature/pcbi1006826-verify/). THE WET-LAB LAYER, all three components confirmed in Methods: (1) qRT-PCR on an independent cohort of nine samples — "Frozen tissue from five SS and four MPNSTs was retrieved from our archive and anonymized"; (2) IHC on "one existing tissue microarray (TMA) and one newly constructed TMA," with "seventy leiomyosarcomas... scored for HMMR protein expression," scored blinded by a pathologist; (3) cell-viability assays with two HDAC inhibitors (quisinostat, trichostatin A; PrestoBlue, 72 h) in four lines SYO-1, JA192, LMS04, LMS05. Ethics: "handled according to... the Code for Proper Secondary Use of Human Tissue in the Netherlands... as reviewed and approved by the LUMC ethical board (B17.036)." THE PORTABLE LAYER: TCGA RNA-seq (206 revised STS cases, NIH GDC, downloaded Feb 2018), GTEx, and French Sarcoma Group arrays from GEO accession GSE21050 (public since June 2010); tooling is R/TensorFlow/Keras, randomForest, Rtsne, caret, limma, maxstat, EnrichR — all $0 and open. TWO NECESSARY QUALIFICATIONS: (a) 'every major computational finding was wet-lab backed' overstates degree — the t-SNE/DNN finding that SS and MPNST resemble nervous-system tissue was never wet-lab validated, and only HMMR of the prognostic gene set went to IHC; the authors themselves hedge to "When possible, we verified our findings in independent datasets or in cell lines." (b) 'the validation is what MADE IT PUBLISHABLE at this level' is an UNVERIFIABLE COUNTERFACTUAL about editorial requirements — PLOS Computational Biology publishes purely computational papers routinely. The load-bearing, verified fact is that the validation layer required assets an unaffiliated solo researcher cannot obtain; whether the paper would have been rejected without it is not established. A separate claim asserting exact public-data cohort sizes (GTEx v7 9,662 samples; GSE21050 DDLPS n=62, LMS n=84) split 1-2 and is not carried as confirmed.

findings.claim: For the ultra-rare / small-n problem, the one MEASURED rule in this evidence set is that the sample-size floor is ANALYSIS-TYPE-DEPENDENT, not a single threshold: MPNST with only five TCGA samples was RETAINED in the supervised random-forest diagnostic-marker analysis — and its markers NEURL1, SCD and NPAS1 were qRT-PCR-verified in an independent cohort — but was EXCLUDED OUTRIGHT from the survival/prognostic-gene analysis for that exact reason.
findings.vote: [15] 3-0 on the facts, but the generalisable rule is the surveyor's inference, not the authors'
findings.evidence: Verified against the fetched PLOS manuscript text (CI run 31594360640; origin/literature-cache:literature/verify-pcbi1006826/, 109,535 bytes, 27 MPNST hits). Cohort: "...50 dedifferentiated liposarcomas (DDLPS), 44 undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcomas (UPS), 17 myxofibrosarcomas (MFS), 10 synovial sarcomas (SS...) and 5 malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumors (MPNST)." Retained in classification: Fig 2b — "Random forests were generated to differentiate between STLMS and ULMS, SS and MPNST, DDLPS and MFS with UPS and last between MFS and UPS. Within the three identified groups a prediction accuracy of over 95% was reached, except when differentiating between UPS and MFS (88%)." Excluded from time-to-event: "We identified prognostic genes for all annotated soft tissue sarcoma subtypes, except MPNST (with only five samples available)." WHY CONFIDENCE IS MEDIUM, NOT HIGH: the paper never articulates a general small-n policy — it simply made that split, and the SS-vs-MPNST classifier rests on 10+5 samples with an UNREPORTED train/test split, so 'n=5 tolerates class discrimination' means 'the authors did it and it survived review', not 'it is statistically sound.' Also note MPNST was not excluded everywhere — it reappears in the CMap therapy step ("Tanespimycin was identified for UPS, ULMS and MPNST"), so the exclusion is specific to the survival analysis. PRACTICAL READ FOR EMC: a supervised discrimination or signature-characterisation claim on a handful of samples is publishable if honestly bounded; a survival or prognostic-gene claim at that n is not.

findings.claim: DERIVED SYNTHESIS FOR THE EMC CASE — of the nine archetypes, three are executable under the stated constraints (unaffiliated, no lab/clinic/IRB/DUA, hundreds of dollars of GPU), one is executable only by admission to an external challenge, and the rest are blocked by specific, nameable constraints rather than by compute.
findings.vote: Not a verified claim — inference built on findings above; the archetypes with no surviving verified evidence are flagged, not asserted
findings.evidence: EXECUTABLE NOW: (2) secondary reanalysis of public molecular data — GDC/cBioPortal/GEO/DepMap are the open tier with no DUA, and the PAK2 paper proves target-nomination clears review on this basis alone; (8) AI/ML on public data, PROVIDED the leakage architecture is adopted (preserved-site CV, released code, honest limitation statement), for which the tooling is free and the authors explicitly justify the method by the unavailability of external cohorts for RARE cancer subtypes; (9) publishable negatives and reproducibility audits, where Lim & Pavlidis is a directly imitable template and the ceiling discipline (decline to adjudicate what the data cannot settle; end in usage recommendations) is the whole credibility architecture. EXECUTABLE ONLY BY ADMISSION: (1) in-silico hit finding with experimental confirmation — the ONLY confirmed no-lab route is a blind prospective challenge where organizers run the assay, and entry is selected, so the blocking constraint is ADMISSION, not compute; without it the ceiling is a hypothesis, and the docking-mill evidence says an unvalidated nomination is now met with prior suspicion. BLOCKED BY ASSETS, NOT COMPUTE: the sarcoma exemplar's validation layer (archival tissue, TMA construction, ethics approval) is unobtainable, so any EMC paper must be designed so that no claim depends on it. TARGET-SPECIFIC BLOCKER FOR EMC: DepMap contains no EMC cell lines, so dependency mining is not directly transferable — the workaround would be fusion-class or cross-disease borrowing, which this evidence set does NOT verify. NOT COVERED BY ANY SURVIVING CLAIM, therefore neither recommended nor excluded here: (3) clinical evidence synthesis / reconstructed IPD from Kaplan-Meier curves, (4) registry epidemiology and what access an unaffiliated individual actually obtains for SEER/NCDB/RARECARE, (5) trial design and external/synthetic control arms, (6) mathematical/mechanistic modelling, (7) hypothesis and perspective papers. Existing repo write-ups of this survey are at /home/user/Rare-cancers/research/manuscripts/no-wet-lab-publication-archetypes.md and the source ledger at /home/user/Rare-cancers/research/literature/no-wet-lab-archetypes-2026-08-12.json.

harness_synthesis.caveats:
COVERAGE IS THE BIGGEST WEAKNESS, AND IT IS UNEVEN BY ARCHETYPE. All 17 surviving claims rest on only SIX primary papers, and they cluster on archetypes 1, 2, 8 and 9. Archetypes 3 (clinical evidence synthesis / Guyot-reconstructed IPD / PROSPERO-PRISMA), 4 (SEER/NCDB/RARECARE registry access for an unaffiliated individual), 5 (basket trials, external control arms, Bayesian borrowing, n-of-1), 6 (adaptive therapy, QSP, dosing/fractionation modelling) and 7 (hypothesis/perspective papers) produced NO claim that survived verification — that is an absence of evidence in this survey, not evidence that those archetypes fail. Any downstream plan that leans on them needs a fresh literature pass.

VERIFICATION WAS DEGRADED BY EGRESS BLOCKING. This environment's proxy blocks nature.com, PMC, PubMed, Europe PMC, Wiley, bioRxiv, Crossref, OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar. Only three claims were confirmed against a genuinely fetched primary full text (the CMap paper and both PLOS Comput Biol claims, all three via GitHub Actions runs 31592017890 / 31594039131 / 31594360640 with artifacts committed to origin/literature-cache), plus the Nat Commun histology paper against a pre-existing repo cache. Everything else — CACHE, the Macip docking review, the Hindawi retraction, the DepMap/PAK2 paper — was confirmed from SEARCH-RESULT RENDERING of the source pages, cross-checked across at least two independent hosts per identifier. That is materially weaker than reading the page. Section-level and figure-panel-level details for those papers are corroborated but not personally read.

ONE FULL TEXT WAS NEVER READ AT ALL. For Sannigrahi et al. (PAK2/DepMap) the Methods section was unobtainable, so whether the PUBLISHED version contains author-generated wet-lab validation is UNVERIFIED. The indirect evidence (deposited code + gene lists only; preprint described as using public data without new experiments; the inhibitor arm explicitly reusing GDSC assays) favours it being a pure reanalysis, but it is not established. Do not cite it as a confirmed zero-wet-lab exemplar without checking the Methods.

EIGHT CLAIMS WERE REFUTED AND SOME WERE ATTRACTIVE. Notably: that CACHE prices validation at ~$25,000/100 compounds and covers it for every qualified participant (0-3); that the prize-winning GNINA workflow is directly executable by a solo researcher on a few hundred dollars of GPU (0-3); that neither docking score nor MM-GBSA could separate actives from inactives at all (0-3 — discrimination actually improved when covalent/noncovalent were separated, best AUC 0.744); and specific CMap rank-migration numbers for parbendazole/withaferin-A/amylocaine/salbutamol (0-3). These must not re-enter the write-up.

THREE CLAIMS CARRY SCOPE OVERREACH THAT WAS CORRECTED HERE AND MUST TRAVEL WITH THEM: the preserved-site CV result is measured on TCGA WHOLE-SLIDE IMAGES only, not all TCGA-derived predictors; the Hindawi retraction's grounds are publication-process integrity for THAT paper, while the genre has separately been criticised on methodological grounds (Front Pharmacol 2026, DOI 10.3389/fphar.2026.1566772); and 'the validation is what made the sarcoma paper publishable' is an unverifiable counterfactual, since PLOS Comput Biol publishes purely computational work.

TWO CLAIMS WERE 2-1 SPLITS: the CACHE data-withholding/blindness mechanism (the verifier corrected the 'cycle 2' terminology — modern CACHE calls these Round 1 and Round 2 within a challenge, and cross-participant withholding protects Round 2 independence rather than making Round 1 blind), and the preserved-site CV statistics (confidence capped at medium by the verifier because the quote's only reachable home was the repo's own cache, i.e. circular provenance).

TIME-SENSITIVITY IS LOW BUT NOT ZERO. Most claims describe what a fixed published document reported, which does not decay. The exceptions are the ones that describe an ONGOING programme or a moving policy: CACHE's admission rules, cost-coverage and target list change per challenge (Challenge #3 on the SARS-CoV-2 Nsp3 macrodomain is now published, and Conscience became steward in 2024); DepMap releases new quarterly data and cell lines; and journal policies on requiring experimental validation were NOT verified from any journal's stated policy page — no such policy text was retrieved in this survey, so every statement about 'which journals accept the archetype' is inferred from where the exemplars were published, not from an editorial policy.
open_questions: What are the actual entry requirements for CACHE for an UNAFFILIATED SOLO participant — is admission open on application, is there any institutional-affiliation or eligibility requirement, and who bears the compound-procurement and assay cost in the current round? The specific cost/coverage claim was refuted 0-3, so this is genuinely unresolved and it is the single highest-leverage question, because CACHE is the only confirmed route to organizer-run wet-lab confirmation of a no-lab prediction.

What do confirmed exemplars look like for the five archetypes with zero surviving evidence — reconstructed-IPD meta-analysis via the Guyot algorithm from published Kaplan-Meier curves, SEER/NCDB/RARECARENet access for an individual with no institutional signature, external/synthetic control arms and Bayesian borrowing for ultra-rare cancers, mathematical/mechanistic modelling, and hypothesis papers? Registry access in particular is a binary gate (some require an institutional signature or a data-use agreement) and it was never checked.

Do the journals that published these exemplars have STATED policies on requiring experimental validation? Nothing in this survey retrieved a policy page; PLOS Computational Biology publishing a wet-lab-backed paper does not establish that it requires one, and knowing the stated policy of PLOS Comput Biol, Molecular Oncology, Scientific Reports, J Chem Inf Model and the sarcoma-specific journals would determine where an EMC paper can be aimed.

For EMC specifically: how many molecular samples exist in PUBLIC repositories worldwide (GEO/SRA/cBioPortal/TCGA-SARC), and is there any EMC or NR4A3-fusion cell line in DepMap or the Cell Model Passports? The DepMap-mining archetype is blocked by cell-line absence rather than by publishability, so the answer decides whether fusion-class pooling or cross-disease borrowing is a workaround or a dead end. Relatedly, has anyone published a small-n Bayesian hierarchical or fusion-class-pooled analysis in sarcoma that passed review, which would give a citable methodological precedent for the n=5-50 regime?

refuted.claim: The paper states, from a ~50-author public-private consortium including industry, that as of 2022 no computational method could reliably find potent drug-like binders, that no CASP-style computational-chemistry benchmark was operational, and that the reason prospective experimental testing of predictions had not been organised was cost — which is the field-level justification for why an unvalidated in-silico hit-finding paper is not taken at face value.

CACHE puts a hard price on experimental validation of computational predictions — ~$25,000 USD per 100 compounds, fully loaded — and in its first two competitions covers that cost for every qualified participant, meaning a computational-only researcher can obtain wet-lab validation of their predictions at zero personal cost initially, with costs transferred to participants in later rounds.

Neither docking scores nor MM-GBSA ΔG values could separate compounds with experimental Mpro inhibitory activity from 113 experimentally confirmed inactive compounds, so a docking-score cutoff cannot legitimately be used to nominate hits or to rank a candidate's potency against a reference — this is the explicit ceiling on what a docking-only paper may claim.

A competitive, prize-winning result in this archetype was achieved with an entirely open-source, modest-compute workflow: GNINA (open-source deep-learning docking) applied to ~7 million commercially available molecules in one arm plus pharmacophore screening in the other, with ranking based on docking scores alone — no proprietary software, no in-house assay data. This is directly executable by an unaffiliated solo researcher with a few hundred dollars of GPU time. [Retrieved via search-result rendering; source domain egress-blocked.]

This is not an isolated case: the same retraction genre spans many sibling 'network pharmacology and/or molecular docking' papers across multiple Hindawi journals retracted in 2023, with PMC identifiers returned in the same searches (e.g. PMC10396634 spinal cord injury; PMC10791440 Picrorhizae Rhizoma anticancer; PMC10632048 Osthole gastric cancer; PMC10718706 Banxia Xiexin decoction; PMC10769737 lung adenocarcinoma; PMC10412194 bladder urothelial carcinoma), establishing that a whole in-silico-only sub-genre has been discredited at scale and that reviewers now treat its template with prior suspicion.

Previously published CMap 1 hits that the original authors had experimentally validated fail to be re-prioritized by CMap 2 even under deliberately favourable, cell-line- and compound-matched comparison: parbendazole went from rank 1 in CMap 1 to rank 142 in CMap 2 (tau = 16.12), withaferin-A from 9 to 196, amylocaine from 20 to 122, and salbutamol from inverse-rank 1 to 61 — i.e. a wet-lab-validated computational hit is not recoverable from the successor version of the same resource.

The standard mitigation used in the digital-pathology literature — stain colour normalization and colour augmentation — does not remove the site signature; site remains predictable at average OVR AUROC above 0.850 under every normalization method tested.

The entire discovery layer of this PLOS Comput Biol paper rested on reused public data: TCGA soft-tissue sarcoma RNA-seq (206 revised cases, downloaded Feb 2018 from the NIH GDC portal), GTEx v7 (9,662 samples across 31 tissue types), and French Sarcoma Group expression arrays pulled from GEO accession GSE21050 (DDLPS n=62, LMS n=84) — i.e., a solo-executable, $0 data footprint for the computational half of the study.

What was established is a clean split: archetype (A) is genuinely executable by an unaffiliated solo researcher at ~$0, because reconstruction of individual patient data from published Kaplan-Meier curves (IPDfromKM, Liu/Zhou/Lee 2021) operates only on published figures and their at-risk tables, requiring no patient contact, IRB or data-use agreement — with a specific, checkable statistical trap to avoid when pooling tiny series (Freeman-Tukey double-arcsine back-transformation is documented to return values and confidence limits of exactly zero at small n, with GLMM the recommended alternative). Archetype (B) is largely CLOSED at the point of access and further limited in what it could answer even if opened: the NCDB Participant User File is restricted by first-party policy (Terms of Agreement stamped "Last Updated: May 2026") to investigators affiliated with a CoC-accredited cancer program, a hard eligibility gate rather than a fee or IRB hurdle; and SEER's treatment fields are confined to first-course therapy and collapse "did not receive" with "unknown" for radiation and chemotherapy, so no salvage/second-line question and no clean untreated-vs-treated denominator is recoverable. The concrete first step for this researcher is therefore archetype (A): assemble every published EMC/NR4A3 Kaplan-Meier figure, check each for a numbers-at-risk table (which determines reconstruction fidelity, not legality), and reconstruct IPD — but the EMC-specific figure census that step depends on remains unanswered by this run.

findings.claim: Archetype (A) is executable with no institutional access: IPDfromKM (Liu N, Zhou Y, Lee JJ, BMC Med Res Methodol 2021;21:111) defines a two-stage workflow — Stage 1 extracts raw coordinates from a published Kaplan-Meier figure, Stage 2 reconstructs individual patient data — whose inputs are published figures and published aggregate numbers only, so it requires no patient contact, no IRB and no data-use agreement. Reconstruction FIDELITY, however, depends on ancillary published quantities (numbers at risk at 5-10 time points, total patients, total events); these are optional arguments, so the method runs on coordinates alone but degrades materially without them. This makes the presence of an at-risk table a QUALITY precondition, never a legal or access one.
findings.evidence: Identifiers cross-agree on four independent hosts (PubMed PMID 34074267; PMC8168323; biomedcentral.com and link.springer.com both serving DOI 10.1186/s12874-021-01308-8; scholar listing giving volume 21, page 111). Abstract wording — 'an easy-to-use, two-stage approach to reconstruct individual patient data (IPD) from published Kaplan-Meier (K-M) curves, where Stage 1 extracts raw data coordinates and Stage 2 reconstructs IPD' — reproduced across three independent search renderings written by different queries. Method: search-result rendering ONLY; every direct fetch (biomedcentral, springer, PMC, PubMed, CRAN, ResearchSquare, scite.ai, OpenAlex, Crossref, Semantic Scholar, MD Anderson Pure) returned EGRESS_BLOCKED or a 403 at the proxy CONNECT layer, so the quote is UNVERIFIED-verbatim. An adversarial search for access-side objections (IRB, DUA, figure-rights permission) found NONE — every documented criticism retrieved concerns ACCURACY (digitization operator error, preprocessing error degrading reconstructed HRs/CIs, algorithm non-convergence, single-analyst reconstruction risk), not permission.

findings.claim: When pooling tiny published rare-cancer series as proportions, the Freeman-Tukey double-arcsine transformation is a documented hazard rather than a safe default: back-transforming a pooled FT estimate can be seriously misleading, and the primary methods paper concludes the transformation should be used only with special caution for meta-analysis of single proportions, with generalized linear mixed models named as the promising alternative and a sensitivity analysis over other sample sizes called mandatory.
findings.evidence: VERIFIED BY DIRECT FETCH, not snippet: the sandbox proxy 403s PubMed/PMC/Europe PMC/OpenAlex/Crossref/doi.org, so retrieval was routed through a GitHub Actions runner (fetch-literature.yml, run 31608213313, completed success with a known-positive PMID assertion that would have failed the build had Europe PMC not returned PMID 30945438). Two independent retrievals agree: Europe PMC core metadata abstract and the PMC OA full text PMC6767151.txt. Full-text Discussion line 41: 'the Freeman-Tukey double arcsine transformation should only be used with special caution for the meta-analysis of single proportions due to potential problems in the back-transformation of meta-analysis results. In our view, a sensitivity analysis using other sample sizes is mandatory for this transformation. GLMMs seem to be a promising alternative.' Record: Schwarzer G, Chemaitelly H, Abu-Raddad LJ, Rücker G, Research Synthesis Methods 2019, 'Seriously misleading results using inverse of Freeman-Tukey double arcsine transformation in meta-analysis of single proportions', Brief Method Note, CC-BY; PMID/DOI/PMCID cross-agree inside the fetched full-text header. Directly on point for rare-cancer pooling: the demonstration case is literally five studies.

findings.claim: The failure mechanism of Freeman-Tukey back-transformation is specific and checkable rather than vague: back-transformation requires substituting a single sample size, and the harmonic mean degenerates across studies of very unequal size. In the published case study, sample sizes ranged from 29 to more than 200,000, the harmonic mean was 85, and back-transformed prevalences AND confidence limits came out exactly equal to zero; in that analysis, sample sizes between about 10 and 120 returned exactly zero.
findings.evidence: Source quote: 'The results using the inverse of the Freeman-Tukey double arcsine transformation based on the harmonic mean of 85 are highly irregular with HCV prevalences and confidence limits exactly equal to zero ... the harmonic mean of 85 is "obviously the wrong choice" in this meta-analysis with sample sizes ranging from 29 to more than 200,000 ... For sample sizes between 10 and around 120, results are exactly zero.' Every numeric element of the claim appears verbatim in the quote; the two interpretive additions (that the inverse double-arcsine is a function of n and so a pooled estimate needs one n substituted; that 'degenerates' renders 'highly irregular' plus 'obviously the wrong choice') are correct statements of Miller's inverse double-arcsine. Confidence capped at medium: the verifying voter could run no search or fetch (WebSearch budget exhausted at 200/200; all nine cross-check hosts EGRESS_BLOCKED), so the PMID-to-text binding for THIS quote rests on the submitting pass, and the ~10-to-~120 zero-window is NOT a universal property of the transformation — its endpoints depend on the pooled double-arcsine value in that specific meta-analysis. The window figure must stay inside its case-study frame or it becomes false as stated.

findings.claim: SEER cannot answer treatment-sequence questions for a rare sarcoma: registry treatment data is limited to FIRST COURSE therapy (chemotherapy, hormonotherapy, immunotherapy, radiation, surgery, or a decision to initiate active surveillance), so no post-progression, relapse, second-line or salvage therapy is abstracted. First-course multimodality sequencing (neoadjuvant chemo to surgery to adjuvant RT) is partially recoverable; later lines are recoverable only through SEER-Medicare linked claims, a separate product requiring an institutional application and DUA and therefore out of reach for an unaffiliated individual.
findings.evidence: Custodian text: 'SEER treatment data is currently limited to the first course treatment modalities, and the time from diagnosis to treatment is the time to the first course treatment, which could be chemotherapy, hormonotherapy, immunotherapy, radiation therapy, surgery, or decision to initiate active surveillance.' The quote nearly tautologically entails the claim; the modality list in the claim is a verbatim restatement. Source is the primary data custodian and the assertion is among the most routinely restated caveats in SEER-based epidemiology, so a single primary source is proportionate. Currency is low-risk — this is a stable structural property of registry abstraction and the source's own wording is 'currently limited'. WEAKNESSES that cap confidence at medium: retrieval was search-snippet rendering on ONE host (seer.cancer.gov EGRESS_BLOCKED to direct fetch) with no second-host cross-check, and the verifier could obtain no contradicting evidence because WebSearch was exhausted and every candidate host was blocked — an absent reading, not a reading of absence. The original claim's absolutism ('a hard ceiling on ANY treatment-sequence question') was narrowed by the verifier to subsequent-line/relapse/salvage specifically, and that narrowed wording is what is reported here.

findings.claim: SEER's radiation and chemotherapy fields cannot distinguish 'did not receive' from 'unknown' — the two are collapsed into one category — so no clean untreated-vs-treated denominator can be constructed in SEER for those modalities. Surgery is NOT affected in the same way, because SEER carries a separate 'Reason no cancer-directed surgery' field.

No separate 'No' or 'None' level exists in either variable. Currency: the corroborating dictionary is the November 2024 SEER*Stat release, with sibling repos referencing 'RX Summ--Surg Prim Site (1998-2022)' and 2023-adjusted income, so the structure persists in current releases. Confidence held at medium because the vote was split 2-1 and the primary page itself was never fetched; the auxiliary cross-reference PMC12599503 cited by the submitting pass is UNVERIFIED.

This run was commissioned to close archetypes 3-7 (C trial design and external control arms, D mathematical/mechanistic modelling, E hypothesis and perspective papers) and to answer three named open questions. It returned ZERO verified claims for C, D and E, and ZERO for all three named questions — CACHE entry requirements for an unaffiliated solo participant, journal experimental-validation policy text, and the EMC/NR4A3 public-repository sample and cell-line census. The seven surviving claims all sit inside (A) and (B). The gap is therefore unchanged for more than half the commissioned scope, and any downstream statement about C, D or E remains inferred rather than sourced.

ENVIRONMENTAL CONSTRAINTS SHAPED WHAT SURVIVED, AND THEY BIASED TOWARD (A) AND (B). The egress proxy blocked direct fetches to nature.com, PMC, PubMed, Europe PMC, Wiley, Crossref, ScienceDirect, Springer, CRAN, seer.cancer.gov, facs.org, OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar and the DuckDuckGo/Bing HTML endpoints, returning 403 at the CONNECT layer. Two claims were rescued by routing fetches through a GitHub Actions runner (the Freeman-Tukey paper via Europe PMC and PMC OA full text; the NCDB pages via direct HTTP 200 reads) — those are the strongest evidence here. Everything else is search-result rendering.

RETRIEVAL METHOD PER FINDING, STATED PLAINLY. Direct page read on an unrestricted runner: Freeman-Tukey (finding 2), NCDB PUF (finding 6). Search-result rendering with multi-host identifier cross-check: IPDfromKM (finding 1) — identifiers confirmed on four hosts, quote UNVERIFIED-verbatim. Search-result rendering, SINGLE host, no cross-check: SEER first-course limitation (finding 4). Search-result rendering plus independent structural corroboration on github.com over SEER*Stat-generated dictionary files: SEER no/unknown collapse (finding 5) — the primary page itself was never fetched.

SPECIFIC WORDING DEFECTS CARRIED FORWARD. (i) 'Only inputs are a published K-M figure' overstates IPDfromKM — numbers at risk, total patients and total events are optional but materially improve fidelity, and preprocessing can fail to converge without them; this affects reconstruction QUALITY, never legal executability. (ii) The '~10 to ~120 returns exactly zero' Freeman-Tukey window is NOT a universal property; its endpoints depend on the pooled double-arcsine value in that one case study, and lifting it out of the case-study frame makes it false. (iii) The original SEER claim's 'any treatment-sequence question' was narrowed to subsequent-line/relapse/salvage; first-course multimodality sequencing IS partially recoverable, and SEER-Medicare linked claims DO capture later lines (that qualification is UNVERIFIED-by-fetch, healthcaredelivery.cancer.gov being blocked). (iv) One sentence attributed to the NCDB /puf/ landing page appears in neither that page nor the Terms PDF and belongs to the separate DUA document — it must be re-anchored or dropped. (v) The NCDB gate blocks the APPLICANT; an unaffiliated person as named personnel on a CoC-affiliated investigator's application is not foreclosed. (vi) PMC12599503, cited as a second host for the SEER collapse, is UNVERIFIED.

TIME-SENSITIVITY. The NCDB terms are stamped May 2026 and reference a June 2026 RFA, so that finding is current but reissued per data-release cycle and should be re-checked before any submission. SEER's structure is stable and the collapse was confirmed against the November 2024 SEER*Stat release. IPDfromKM remains live on CRAN (manual dated 21 July 2025). The Freeman-Tukey conclusion is a 2019 statement of a paper's own content and cannot go stale, though the wider methodological consensus has since moved further toward GLMM/logit defaults, which strengthens rather than weakens it.

SEVERAL PLAUSIBLE-LOOKING CLAIMS WERE REFUTED AND MUST NOT BE REINTRODUCED, notably: that SEER's Research Plus tier rejects free/personal email providers by name; that SEER itself explicitly forbids comparative-effectiveness analysis; that NCDB requires a Cancer Committee Chair letterhead signature; specific accuracy benchmarks and corpus sizes from a 2025 Contemporary Clinical Trials Communications reconstruction-methods paper (two search renderings gave CONFLICTING DOIs for the same article); and specific case counts from a 2025 Neurosurgical Review case-report pooling exemplar. [Search-result rendering only; page fetch blocked — UNVERIFIED-verbatim.]

The paper's credibility architecture is benchmarking against known quantities rather than assertion: the authors validate reconstruction accuracy for event counts, numbers at risk, survival probabilities, median survival times and hazard ratios via simulation plus real-data application. [Search-result rendering only; page fetch blocked — UNVERIFIED-verbatim.]

The tooling is free, public and requires no institutional software licence: an open R package (IPDfromKM, on CRAN) plus a hosted web Shiny application (search results give the host as https://www.trialdesign.org, and an app user guide by Zhou, Liu and Lee at biostatistics.mdanderson.org), covering extraction, reconstruction, visualisation, accuracy assessment and secondary analysis in one pipeline — i.e. archetype A is executable at ~$0 by a solo unaffiliated researcher. The paper reports an empirical accuracy benchmark: reconstructed hazard ratios reproduced published HRs closely, with mean and median absolute percentage differences of 2.85% and 2.14% across 58 reconstructed hazard ratios. CAUTION — the two independent search renderings disagree on the corpus size ('46 published KM curves' in one, '58 reconstructed IPD and corresponding hazard ratio estimates' in the other); the 2.85%/2.14% figures appeared in only ONE rendering and are UNVERIFIED.

The paper states a concrete, checkable limitation of curve reconstruction: fidelity is conditional on the graphical quality of the published curve (noise) and on correct preprocessing of the extracted coordinates — meaning reconstruction error is driven by figure quality, not only by the reconstruction algorithm. This is directly relevant to rare-cancer/sarcoma series, whose KM figures are often small, low-resolution and heavily censored. UNVERIFIED (search rendering only).

Formal pooling of individual patient data drawn from published case reports is a peer-reviewed, publishable method for ultra-rare tumours: this 2025 Neurosurgical Review paper (Zuo P, Zou W, Wang Y, et al., Neurosurg Rev 48:543, DOI 10.1007/s10143-025-03704-w) combined 7 institutional cases with 17 cases extracted from the literature into a single 24-patient IPD analysis. NOTE: title/DOI/journal confirmed on two independent hosts (Springer Nature Link result listing and Google/Bing-rendered search summaries); abstract text obtained via search-result rendering only, as link.springer.com, api.semanticscholar.org and ouci.dntb.gov.ua are all blocked by this environment's proxy.

For an ultra-rare entity, the entire world literature usable for pooling can be on the order of 17 published cases spanning ~35 years, and single case reports are accepted as IPD units — i.e. no minimum-n inclusion floor was applied to the included publications. This directly answers whether aggregation of case reports is respected practice at the extreme tail of rarity (the EMC/NR4A3 situation).

The paper's stated premise is that case reports are routinely excluded from systematic reviews while rare-disease patients depend disproportionately on individualized strategies — i.e. it is a published, peer-reviewed argument that case-report evidence has legitimate standing in rare-disease evidence synthesis, which is exactly the methodological warrant question (A) asks about for ultra-rare tumours. UNVERIFIED as verbatim text: this is search-engine rendering of the abstract, not fetched source prose.

A directly relevant companion paper exists and is a stronger exemplar for question (A) than this source: "Agreement between results of meta-analyses from case reports and clinical studies, regarding efficacy and safety of idursulfase therapy in patients with mucopolysaccharidosis type II (MPS-II). A new tool for evidence-based medicine in rare diseases", Orphanet J Rare Dis, DOI 10.1186/s13023-019-1202-6, PMC6805333 — i.e. a published formal meta-analysis OF CASE REPORTS whose results were benchmarked against a meta-analysis of clinical studies. Identifier seen on three independent hosts (ojrd.biomedcentral.com, link.springer.com, ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc). Full text not fetched (all three hosts blocked), so its methods, pooling model and quality-assessment tools remain unread.

The failure occurs precisely in the regime a rare-cancer pooling exercise occupies — few studies, small n, near-boundary proportions. The five-study case study had HCV prevalence ranging 0% to 18.4% with a median of 0.5%, and the paper fits generalized linear mixed models with a logit link alongside the transformation-based generic inverse-variance analyses, making a GLMM the documented alternative when Freeman-Tukey back-transformation is unsafe.

SEER Research Plus (the tier carrying the more detailed case-level fields) requires user authentication through an eRA Commons or HHS account, and that account must be tied to an institutional email address (.edu, .gov, .org, or work address) — meaning an unaffiliated solo researcher cannot authenticate at all for the Research Plus tier. RETRIEVAL CAVEAT: seer.cancer.gov is blocked by this environment's egress proxy; the target page was never fetched. Text below is search-result rendering, corroborated across three independent queries in which access.html was a returned hit.

SEER explicitly rejects requests submitted from free/personal email providers (Gmail, iCloud, 163.com are named), and requires an email address affiliated with a self-identified institution or corporation — an affiliation gate, not merely a contact-address preference. This is the single decisive fact for archetype (B) for an unaffiliated individual. RETRIEVAL CAVEAT: search-result rendering only; direct fetch blocked.

Institutional affiliation for SEER data access is verified through NIH/HHS identity infrastructure administered by the Office of Data Sharing — specifically eRA Commons accounts or HHS PIV cards — and all correspondence about the request and its approval uses the institutional email. This means the affiliation requirement is enforced by a federal identity system, not by self-attestation on a form, so it cannot be satisfied by a solo researcher asserting independent-researcher status. RETRIEVAL CAVEAT: search-result rendering only; direct fetch blocked.

SEER itself explicitly advises against comparative-effectiveness analysis and outcome comparisons conditioned on treatment, because determinants of treatment (patient preference, physician recommendation, comorbidity, provider proximity) are not captured in the registry — i.e. the archetype 'compare treatment A vs B in SEER for a rare sarcoma' is disallowed by the data owner, not merely difficult. [Search-result rendering of the Nov 2023 submission page]

The application requires an institutional signature that a solo researcher cannot self-supply: a letter of support on hospital or cancer-program letterhead from the Cancer Committee Chair on record with the CoC (or, if the applicant is the Chair, from the Cancer Program Administrator), plus a 2-page-or-less biosketch.

Facility-level and geographic questions are not recoverable from the PUF: the file is de-identified beyond 45 CFR 164.514, does not identify hospitals or providers, and geographic information is deliberately excluded — though aggregated patient characteristics (education, income, travel distance) and facility characteristics are retained.
